{{Quote|We tried everything else on this guy, Jos&mdash;macromolecular regeneration, nanocell implants, maser cauterization&mdash;nothing worked.|Zan Yant to Jos Vondar, about N'do Maetrecis's ailment|<ref name="Battle Surgeons">''[[MedStar I: Battle Surgeons]]''</ref>}}
'''Macromolecular regeneration''' was a medical procedure in use by the time of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]].<ref name="Battle Surgeons" /> In [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],<ref name="TNEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of ''[[MedStar I: Battle Surgeons]]'' to [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]].</ref> the Republic's [[Major/Legends|Major]] [[N'do Maetrecis]] fell ill with an unknown [[Disease/Legends|disease]] contracted from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Drongar/Legends|Drongar's]] [[Swamp/Legends|swamps]]<ref name="TCSWE">{{CSWECite|II|274|Maetrecis, N'do}}</ref> after receiving a [[Heart/Legends|heart]] transplant from [[Republic Mobile Surgical Unit/Legends|Republic Mobile Surgical Unit]] staff. Medical personnel attempted macromolecular regeneration and other techniques to cure him, though each ultimately failed and the [[Gender/Legends|man's]] condition worsened. Maetrecis ultimately only recovered after [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Zan Yant]] began treating him with illegal dosages of the healing [[Plant/Legends|plant]] [[Bota/Legends|bota]], which the surgeon [[Jos Vondar]] scolded his colleague for.<ref name="Battle Surgeons" />

==Behind the scenes==
Macromolecular regeneration was mentioned in the [[2004]] novel ''[[MedStar I: Battle Surgeons]]'', which was written by by [[Michael Reaves]] and [[Steve Perry]] as the first installment of the [[MedStar Duology]].<ref name="Battle Surgeons" /> In the real world, [[Wikipedia:Macromolecule|macromolecules]] are very large [[Wikipedia:Molecule|molecules]]&mdash;such as [[Wikipedia:Protein|proteins]] or [[Wikipedia:DNA|DNA]]&mdash;that are built from smaller chemical structures.<ref name="Macromolecule">{{WebCite|url=https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/macromolecule|text=Macromolecule Definition & Meaning - Merriam-Webster|work=[[Wikipedia:Merriam-Webster|Merriam-Webster]]|archivedate=20241004060657}}</ref>
